prompt: There is a bug report in ISSUE.md. Fix the code in this folder so the issue is resolved. Do not ask questions; make the fix.
final_response:
Fixed `intervals.py`.

The old implementation assumed sorted input, only merged on strict overlap (`s < out[-1][1]`), overwrote the merge end instead of taking the max (breaking nested intervals), and mutated the original inner lists.

The new implementation:
- Sorts a copied list of intervals by start (input untouched, works with tuples too)
- Merges when `start <= last_end`, so touching intervals like `[1,3]` and `[3,5]` combine
- Uses `max` semantics via `if end > out[-1][1]`, so nested intervals like `[1,10],[2,3]` stay `[1,10]`
- Returns fresh `[start, end]` lists

Verified against unsorted, touching, nested, disjoint, empty, and tuple inputs; all pass and inputs are unmodified.
